up.note: An exact characterisation, not merely a polynomial relation: nondeterministic quantum query complexity is half the nondeterministic degree. The acceptance amplitude of a $T$-query algorithm is a degree-$2T$ polynomial nonzero exactly on the $1$-inputs, and conversely $p$ may be rescaled by its maximum over the cube; nonvanishing is scale-invariant and off-domain behaviour is unconstrained either way, so this is a statement about partial functions.

Upper bounds — holds for every partial

  • \(\mathrm{NQ}(f) = \lceil \mathrm{ndeg}(f)/2\rceil\)
    deWolf03
    An exact characterisation, not merely a polynomial relation: nondeterministic quantum query complexity is half the nondeterministic degree. The acceptance amplitude of a $T$-query algorithm is a degree-$2T$ polynomial nonzero exactly on the $1$-inputs, and conversely $p$ may be rescaled by its maximum over the cube; nonvanishing is scale-invariant and off-domain behaviour is unconstrained either way, so this is a statement about partial functions.

Also $\mathrm{ndeg}(f)\le\mathrm{C}^{1}(f)$, and $\mathrm{ndeg}$ can be exponentially smaller than $\mathrm{D}$ -- the nondeterministic world is genuinely different.

see also: \(\mathrm{NQ}(f)\), \(\mathrm{ndeg}(f)\), \(\mathrm{C}^1(f)\) data/relations/03-quantum.yaml
